newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. Times 2nd quarter aided by newspaper group.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. Times 2nd quarter aided by newspaper group.

text.p: The New York Times Co., parent of The New York Times and The Boston Globe, Thursday reported higher second-quarter earnings, aided by strength in its newspaper group.

The media company said operating profits in its newspaper group were $119.4 million, up from $86.6 million a year earlier. Its broadcast group had profits of $11.9 milllion, up from $8.2 million, and the magazine group had profits of $9.2 million, up from $6.5 million a year earlier.
The company said the increase in the newspaper group's revenues was primarily the result of higher advertising revenues from higher rates and volume.
For the quarter, the company earned $84.9 million, or 85 cents a share, on revenues of $721.9 million. A year earlier, it earned $46.8 million, or 48 cents a share, on revenues of $649.5 million.

The company also said revenue and operating profit increases at the broadcasting group were principally the result of the acquisition of two NBC affiliates that were acquired in July 1996, as well as stronger advertising revenues at WTKR-TV in Norfolk, Va.
The two new stations contributed $3.6 million of operating profit in the quarter.

In addition, the company said the magazine group's operating profit increase was primarily the result of higher advertising revenues from higher ad volume at Golf Co., partially offset by increased losses associated with new ventures.
New York Times stock lost 87.5 cents to $52.375 in midday trading on the American Stock Exchange.
